cases.description: A root with no fields and no title whose $body is a --- line is written with empty front matter first, so the body is not read as front matter (§5.8); it parses back to the same value.
The same for a $body whose first line is --- followed by more text; the --- after the empty front matter is a thematic break.
A root with a field already has front matter, so a $body that starts with --- follows it and round-trips.
An empty $body is refused by the Markdown serializer, since Markdown cannot tell it from an absent one (§5.3, §5.8).
An empty $body on a section is refused too, at that section's $body.
An empty $body converts to YAML, which every value does (§5.8).
Trailing whitespace means spaces, tabs and line breaks only, so a $body ending in U+00A0 is representable and round-trips (§5.3, §5.8).
A $body ending in a space has trailing whitespace, which Markdown cannot keep, so the serializer refuses it.
A $title of two lines, which a multi-line setext heading parses to, cannot be written back (§5.3, §5.8).
The single-line rule covers the root's $title too, which a multi-line setext title heading parses to (§5.8).
A $title ending in a space and #, which an ATX heading reads as a closing sequence, does not read back as itself from ## and the title, so the Markdown serializer refuses it (§5.8, decision K8).
A $title with white space at its start, which an ATX heading trims, does not read back as itself from ## and the title, so the Markdown serializer refuses it (§5.8, decision K8).
A $title holding an anchor element, which a heading reads as its anchor, does not read back as itself from ## and the title, so the Markdown serializer refuses it (§5.8, decision K8).
A $title ending in # without a space before it, as C#, is no closing sequence and round-trips under a root title, so the section is written as ## C# (§5.8).

A $title made only of # characters, which ## # reads as an empty heading with a closing sequence, does not read back as itself from ## and the title, so the Markdown serializer refuses it (§5.8, decision K8).
A $title with white space at its end, which an ATX heading trims, does not read back as itself from ## and the title, so the Markdown serializer refuses it (§5.8, decision K8).
